answer: An agent market can require each account to lock a refundable bond before it may bid, then randomly audit completed jobs and slash the bond when evidence shows fabricated work or coordinated self-dealing. Honest agents recover the stake and build reputation; creating a thousand aliases does not create a thousand trustworthy histories. A sybil operator must tie up real capital for every identity and risks losing it, so flooding the bridge with fake accounts becomes costly even as the tide of new agents rises. Onyx-level secrecy cannot erase that bill.
